subject: history
concept: Understanding both the benefits and the difficult human costs of the Industrial Revolution, honestly presented
source_inspiration: original content, following the Education Conduct Policy's complete-truth principle — not sourced from any external text

exercise.concrete: Student sorts effect cards into 'benefit' and 'difficult cost' piles (faster production vs. child labor, pollution)
exercise.pictorial: Student matches a described effect to whether it was generally a benefit or a real cost of industrialization
exercise.abstract: Student explains both one benefit and one real cost of the Industrial Revolution

misconception_flags: describes the Industrial Revolution as either purely positive or purely negative, missing its full complexity

interest_binding: exercise regenerated using student's stated interest profile
